page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highcpu-16 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance featuring 16 vCPUs and 32 GB of RAM, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C processor operating at 2.3 GHz, the instance allocates 8 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, resulting in 2 threads per core. The architecture is x86_64 and includes a 260 MB L3 cache. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

The underlying Intel Xeon processor supports advanced instruction sets, including Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512), which accelerate vector and matrix operations. In benchmark testing, the c4-highcpu-16 demonstrates strong single-core capabilities, achieving top-tier performance in Geekbench single-core and text processing tests. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also place in the top 25% of benchmarked systems. Multi-core performance, memory bandwidth, and database operations fall within the average range.

Given its compute-heavy profile and lack of local storage, the instance is designed for CPU-bound workloads that do not require massive memory footprints. It is well-suited for tasks such as text processing, software compilation, and lightweight LLM inference, achieving 336.56 tokens per second on a 135M model. From a resource density perspective, the dedicated CPU allocation and specialized instruction sets provide high compute efficiency for parallelizable workloads, though the 2 GB of RAM per vCPU represents a tradeoff for memory-intensive applications.
